newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DEL PIERO DOUBLE KEEPS JUVENTUS ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEL PIERO DOUBLE KEEPS JUVENTUS ON TOP.

text.p: European and world club champions Juventus took command of Italy's Serie A on Wednesday when two penalties by striker Alessandro Del Piero helped them to a 4-1 win over Udinese.
The win put Juventus three points clear at the top of the table with Vicenza second on 22 points, Internazionale third on 21 points and Bologna and Napoli a point further back.

Juventus have been in outstanding form with impressive wins over Sampdoria last Sunday after lifting the World Club Cup in Tokyo and victories over England's Manchester United and Turkey's Fenerbahce in the Champions' League.
But they were forced to show their defensive qualities as the home side dominated the opening salvos before Croatian striker Alen Boksic opened the scoring against the run of play after 23 minutes.
On his own in front of goal, Boksic first hit the post before blasting the rebound past a prostrate Luigi Turci in the Udinese goal.

"I thought we were playing better football than them before Boksic scored and his goal kind of knocked the wind out of us," said Udinese's German striker Oliver Bierhoff, who is sidelined following knee surgery and had to watch the game from the stands.
Udinese laid siege to Italy keeper Angelo Peruzzi's goal and looked like equalising before Juventus again struck on the counter-attack.

Giovanni Bia hauled down Boksic in the area eight minutes from halftime and Del Piero converted the penalty. Just before the break Del Piero was also brought down inside the box and coolly made it 3-0 with his second penalty.

A gutsy Udinese, who are in the bottom half of the table, showed some pride after the interval and forced Peruzzi to make three consecutive saves before midfielder Massimiliano Cappioli broke through to make it 3-1 nine minutes into the second half.

But Juventus, without Uruguay's Paolo Montero, Dimas of Portugal and Yugoslavia's Vladimir Jugovic, all away on World Cup duty, simply outclassed the north-eastern club and authoritative French midfielder Didier Deschamps settled the issue with a rare goal in the 70th minute.
